newsitem.title: USA: MasterCard transactions up 15 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: MasterCard transactions up 15 percent in 1996.

text.p: MasterCard International said Friday its cardholders used MasterCard cards for a record $552.8 billion worth of transactions worldwide in 1996, up 15 percent from a year earlier.
It was the first time MasterCard has exceeded half a trillion dollars in gross dollar volume in a single year, the global payments systems company said.
MasterCard said cards in circulation at the end of 1996 reached 404.1 million, up from 342.5 million a year earlier,
The 18 percent year-over-year increase reflects growth across all product lines, particularly the Gold MasterCard credit card and the Maestro debit card.
MasterCard cards were used for more than 5.8 billion transactions over the course of the year, up from 5 billion in 1995, the company said.
In the United States, there were 2.7 billion MasterCard transactions, up from 2.4 billion in 1995.
Growth in debit card acceptance was especially strong, MasterCard said. Cards in the MasterMoney off-line debit card programme reached 15.6 million, up 106 percent from 1995.
At year-end 1996, there also were some 94 million Maestro-branded cards in circulation, up 35 percent from year-end 1995. The growth reflects rising consumer demand for debit cards, the company said.
Master-Card's share of single-programme bank card solicitations in the U.S. mail in 1996 jumped to 35 percent, from 26 percent in 1995, according to Mail Monitor.
Mail share is considered a leading indicator of brand market share, MasterCard said.
The number of MasterCard/Cirrus ATMs worldwide rose 20 percent to more than 315,000 locations.
In the past two years, several major U.S. banks, including Chase Manhattan Corp. and Wells Fargo and Co., have converted their debit card portfolios to MasterCard from Visa, the company said.
